text.p: MINNEAPOLIS, June 17 Reuter- Education Alternatives Inc, which has turned its management efforts to private schools from public schools, said it is looking to acquire career colleges to offer students an integrated education program from pre-school through job placement.

"Our focus now is to become a leader in pre-school through career college and that, career college, is a new change for us," John Golle, chairman and founder of Education Alternatives, told a Piper Jaffray investment conference here.
Both of the company's contracts to manage public schools in Baltimore, Maryland, and Hartford, Connecticut, were terminated.

Based on its experience in these and other public school districts, and indications of an evolving acceptance of "private alternative" schools, Golle said the company is seeking to develop or acquire schools which are geographically near each other that will educate a student from pre-kindergarten through a career college.

However, Education Alternatives says specific criteria must be met before it will proceed with a school project. Among other requirements, the company will not provide its services unless it can use its own employees or have complete control over others and unless it can implement its own curriculum.
The company plans to open two college preparatory schools this fall, one in Mays Landing, New Jersey, and one in South Bend, Indiana. Each charge students tuition of $7,300 to $8,500 a year.

Consolidation among career colleges provides an opportunity for the company, he said. "Our focus, and we are well down the road on this, is to acquire high technology career colleges," which will be integrated into the company's high schools, Golle said.
Education Alternatives is looking to acquire colleges in the states where it currently operates -- Arizona, Minnesota, New Jersey and Massachusetts -- so this integration will be successful.
These career colleges acquisition candidates must also have a high placement rate with jobs offering $35,000 or more. "There are a few of these and we are in pursuit of them," he said.

Meanwhile, revenues from the two private schools currently managed by Education Alternatives are expected to reach $4.7 million for the fiscal year to end June 30, 1997, said Gerald Haugen, chief financial officer.

The company also expects to report a profit of $700,000 or $0.09 a share on revenues of about $4.7 million generated by its two private schools in Eagan, Minnesota, and Paradise Valley, Arizona. These schools provide a curriculum for pre-kindergarten through the eigth grade. There are about 260 students in the Minnesota school and about 420 students at the Arizona school.

Estimated profits for its fiscal year to end June 30, 1997 include a payment of about $1.5 million from the company's investment management firm to resolve some issues and a payment of $650,000 from settlement of a contract with the city of Hartford, Haugen said.
